title: Reconstructing a constructible integral sheaf from its positive derived reductions
statement: In the finite-field setting of [sk-def-sf-setting], let X be separated and finite type over the algebraically closed base, and E a finite extension of Q_l, with l different from the characteristic. Let N be a constructible completed-integral sheaf in the sense of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Put K_n = integralReductionFunctor l E X (n+1)(N[0]), the actual derived quotient tensor functor of [def-sfb-integral-derived-coefficient-data]. There is a categorical product of these K_n and transition maps K_(n+1) -> K_n for which N[0] is a derived limit [def-weil-derived-limit].

source.place: paragraph (2): derived completeness and the three finite-reduction bullets

proof.text: Finite type over the affine point gives compactness, and separatedness gives quasi-separatedness. Apply the existing complete_sheaf theorem from QcqsIntegralFiniteModelCompleteness to N. This is the finite-model completeness argument for the actual strict quotient augmentation, and requires neither an embedded coefficient field nor a torsion-free hypothesis. Retain its K-flat representative P, representative isomorphism and invertible augmentation.

Exact countable products of internal pro-etale modules give countable products in their derived category. The principal tensor/scalar-extension comparison identifies each displayed tensor reduction at exponent n+1 with integralLevel n and intertwines the actual quotient transition maps. The componentwise comparison and its inverses induce an isomorphism B of their products. Product extensionality shows that B intertwines the two Roos endomorphisms 1-shift.

Apply roos_isDerivedLimit to the K-flat representative. The completionMap from N[0] to the strict Roos complex is invertible by completeness. Transport the distinguished triangle along this isomorphism in its first vertex and B in its two product vertices. The first arrow is completionMap followed by the old projection and B inverse; the last arrow is B followed by the old connecting arrow and the shifted inverse completionMap. Triangle.isoMk verifies the squares and distinguished_iff_of_iso gives IsDerivedLimit for the displayed tensor tower.

theorem integral_constructible_reduction_limit
    (D : WeilConjectures.FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    (N : pulledBackModuleObjects (integralCoefficientRing l E) X)
    (hN : IsConstantModelConstructible (integralCoefficientRing l E) X N) :
    ∃ hp : HasProduct (fun n : ℕ ↦ (integralReductionFunctor l E X (n + 1)).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj N)),
      let := hp
      ∃ step : ∀ n : ℕ,
        (integralReductionFunctor l E X (n + 2)).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj N) ⟶
          (integralReductionFunctor l E X (n + 1)).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj N),
        IsDerivedLimit (K := fun n : ℕ ↦
          (integralReductionFunctor l E X (n + 1)).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj N)) step
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj N)
